newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 30.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- State prosecutors will summon Chung Tae-soo, founder of the Hanbo Group, and two of his sons Thursday or Friday to investigate allegations of bribing politicians and bankers to obtain preferential loans. Managers of four Seoul banks will also be summoned as early as January 30.
- Two ships for transporting nuclear waste to North Korea have anchored at a port in northern Taipei and are expected to soon move to Lanyu Island southeast of Taipei, where the waste is stored.

- Chinese President Jiang Zemin cited concern over Taiwan's planned shipments of nuclear waste to North Korea in a meeting with the speaker of South Korea's National Assembly. He added China will express its official position on the matter before long.

- State-run Taiwan Power Company, which signed a formal contract with North Korea to take its nuclear waste, has said if North Korea's capabilities to store nuclear waste are not up to standard it will reconsider the deal.
- Seo Sung-ha, a financial executive of Hanbo Group left for Singapore on Saturday, while another official submitted a letter of resignation on Sunday.

- Financial difficulties of local companies which began with nationwide strikes protesting against a new labour law are getting worse. Major banks and securities firms are reluctant to guarantee corporate bond issues.
